**Video:** [Lec 49 — Attention Part 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TGzZ8jCX4y0)

## Learning goals

- Pack Q, K, V into matrices and write **scaled** attention in one formula.
- Explain why we divide by $\sqrt{d_k}$.
- Contrast self-attention, cross-attention, and causal (masked) attention.

## Before this clicks

Lecture 48 did attention one query at a time. Deep learning prefers **batched linear algebra**: stack all queries, keys, and values and compute every score with one matmul. Scaling by $\sqrt{d_k}$ keeps softmax from saturating when dimensions grow.

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Matrix packing

Let $Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d_k}$, $K\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d_k}$, $V\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d_v}$ hold rows $q_i^\top$, $k_j^\top$, $v_j^\top$. For **self-attention**, $n=m$ and all three come from the same sequence.

Score matrix:

$$
S = QK^\top \in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m},\qquad S_{ij}=q_i^\top k_j.
$$

### 2. Scaled dot-product attention

$$
\mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V)=\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V.
$$

Softmax is row-wise: each query’s scores become a distribution over keys, then multiply by $V$.

### 3. Why $\sqrt{d_k}$?

If entries of $q,k$ are roughly unit-scale independent, $q^\top k$ has variance about $d_k$. Large magnitude scores make softmax nearly one-hot and gradients tiny. Dividing by $\sqrt{d_k}$ stabilizes the scale.

### 4. Self vs cross vs causal

| Mode | $Q$ from | $K,V$ from | Typical use |
|------|----------|------------|-------------|
| Self-attention | same sequence | same sequence | encoder / decoder self layers |
| Cross-attention | decoder | encoder memory | encoder–decoder MT |
| Causal / masked | same sequence | same (+ mask) | language modeling |

**Causal mask:** set $S_{ij}=-\infty$ for $j>i$ (future tokens) before softmax so $\alpha_{ij}=0$ for illegal positions.

### 5. Complexity note

Dense self-attention is $O(n^2 d)$ in sequence length $n$ — every pair interacts. That is the price of full connectivity (and the reason for later efficient-attention variants).

---

## Worked mini-example

$n=2$, $d_k=2$, ignore scaling first. Suppose

$$
QK^\top=\begin{bmatrix}2&0\\0&2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Row-softmax $\approx I$, so $\mathrm{Attention}\approx V$: each position almost only reads its own value. If off-diagonals dominate, mass shifts to other positions’ values. Adding $/ \sqrt{2}$ shrinks the $2$s toward milder weights.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Softmax over the whole matrix | Softmax is **per query row**, not global. |
| Scaling changes who wins arbitrarily | It rescales; relative order of scores in a row is unchanged. |
| Mask after softmax | Mask **logits** (set $-\infty$) before softmax so weights renormalize. |
| Cross-attention needs equal lengths | $n$ (queries) and $m$ (keys) may differ. |

4. How do you prevent attending to future tokens?
